To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Innate secretory antibodies, produced by the normal immune system in the absence of antigenic stimulation, provide a first line of defense against microbial infections.
“innate secretory antibodies are produced by the normal gut flora and are important in protecting both the host and the population against infection by Salmonella typhymurium.”
Innate IgA in pIpR−/− knock-out mice is able to bind S. typhymurium in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the polymeric immunoglobulins (pIg) in protection against Salmonella infection.
the innate immune system and its role in the prevention of infectious disease.
the innate immune response of the gastrointestinal tract to bacterial pathogens and the mechanisms of host defense in the intestinal epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
innate secretory antibodies are a critical component of the mucosal immune system and play a major role in protection from enteric pathogens.
the major role for SAbs is to prevent the spread (transmission) of microbes throughout the population, and not to protect local mucosal surfaces.
innate SAbs may have evolved in mammals to prevent the spread and infection of the herd, rather than protection against local infection of the individual.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
innate SAbs are a major component in host defense against infection and that they may have evolved as a major defense against pathogens, rather than against commensal flora.

the polymeric immunoglobulins (pIgs) play an important role in the protection of the host against infection with Salmonella.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SAbs are a key component of innate immune defense against infection and are not merely “passive” bystanders in mucosal immunity.
the innate secretory antibodies may play a role in protection of the population against the spread of pathogens.
